items.request: One-page summary stating what the deal is and the ask in one line: amount, instrument, our allocation, use of proceeds, structure and security.
items.format: Sponsor-written one-pager or deck page 1, dated.
items.why: A deal that cannot be stated in one line usually hides its structure (0.8 deck order item 1).
items.pass: Amount, instrument, allocation, use of proceeds and security are each stated and tie to the sources-and-uses table to the dollar.
items.fail: Ask, instrument or security missing or inconsistent with the model or term sheet.
items.verify: Tie every figure to the sources-and-uses table and the draft term sheet.

items.request: Investor deck in the universal order (ask, problem, asset, sponsor and track record, market and cycle, numbers, structure, returns with sensitivities, risks, terms), with every sponsor claim marked verified (and by whom) or asserted.
items.format: PDF deck plus an editable claims register listing each factual claim, its source document and its verifier.
items.why: Claims presented as fact that nobody independently sourced; investment cases resting on pitch delivery rather than evidence (0.12).
items.pass: Every factual claim appears in the claims register with a source document; every 'verified' claim names a third party we can contact.
items.fail: Claims with no source; 'verified' claims with no named verifier; deck cites round price, a marquee co-investor or a national forecast as validation.
items.verify: Score the written materials and data room before the live pitch with a fixed rubric and more than one rater; contact each named verifier.

items.request: Sources-and-uses table showing every dollar in and out, including all fees, reimbursements and payments to the sponsor, its affiliates or insiders.
items.format: Excel, tied to the model and the draft closing funds flow.
items.why: Insider steering and fee leakage hidden in use of proceeds (0.4 sales-side tells).
items.pass: Sources equal uses; every payment to the sponsor, an affiliate or an insider is itemized and disclosed.
items.fail: Unitemized 'other' or 'working capital' buckets; undisclosed payments to related parties; repayment of sponsor loans not disclosed.
items.verify: Reconcile to the funds-flow memo at closing and to bank statements after funding.

items.request: Live financial model (native Excel, formulas intact) with historicals, a base case and a downside case, and all assumptions on one input tab.
items.format: Native .xlsx with no hard-coded outputs; version-dated.
items.why: Returns that exist only as a PDF output cannot be stress tested (0.6, 0.7 item 5).
items.pass: Model runs, ties to the historical financials, and contains a separately built downside case; no hard-coded outputs.
items.fail: PDF-only model, hard-coded returns, or downside case that is the base case with a small haircut.
items.verify: Rebuild the key outputs ourselves from the input tab; reconcile historicals to bank statements in the QoE.

items.request: Historical financial statements for the last 3 fiscal years and year-to-date (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow), audited where audits exist.
items.format: Auditor-signed statements where audited; otherwise accountant-reviewed or management statements clearly labelled.
items.why: Projections with no verified history; sloppy numbers signal broader governance problems (0.2, 0.8).
items.pass: Statements for every period are provided, internally consistent, and labelled audited, reviewed or management-prepared.
items.fail: Missing periods, unexplained restatements, or adjusted figures with no GAAP reconciliation.
items.verify: Obtain audited statements directly from the auditor with signed authorization; proof of cash in the QoE.

items.request: Government-issued photo ID and proof of residential address for every principal, control person, director, CFO, controller and wire signatory of the sponsor and the issuer.
items.format: Unexpired passport or driver's licence (color copy) plus a utility bill or bank statement under 90 days old; verified by live video or in person.
items.why: Identity fraud, nominee principals and AI-generated identities (0.2, 0.3, 0.4).
items.pass: Every named person has a valid, unexpired ID whose name and date of birth match the background-check report and the entity records.
items.fail: Expired or inconsistent IDs, refusal to produce ID for a control person or wire releaser, or names that do not match entity filings.
items.verify: Run document-authenticity checks through the background-check vendor and confirm identity on a live call initiated by us.

items.request: Formation documents for the sponsor and every entity in the deal chain: certificate of formation or incorporation, operating agreement or bylaws, all amendments, and current good-standing certificates.
items.format: Secretary-of-state certified copies; good-standing certificates dated within 30 days.
items.why: Sham or lapsed entities and undisclosed control rights (0.2, 0.3).
items.pass: Every entity exists, is in good standing, and its governing documents name the same managers and members as the org chart.
items.fail: Entity not found, administratively dissolved, or governing documents naming persons absent from the org chart.
items.verify: Pull each entity record ourselves from the secretary of state of each jurisdiction.

items.request: Certified ownership and organization chart from each ultimate natural-person owner down to the deal vehicle, including every affiliate, principal-owned entity, SPV, JV and side vehicle.
items.format: Chart certified by an officer, with percentage ownership and voting control on every link.
items.why: Hidden affiliates hold assets, debts and pledges the lender never sees (First Brands, 0.4); no federal BOI registry to rely on (0.3, 0.18).
items.pass: Chart reconciles to formation documents, cap tables and operating agreements; every entity on UCC and litigation searches appears on the chart.
items.fail: Entities found in searches that are missing from the chart; circular or nominee ownership; refusal to certify.
items.verify: Reconcile to state filings, UCC search debtor names and our own CDD; there is no federal BOI record for US companies after Aug. 14, 2026.

items.request: Beneficial-ownership certification identifying every natural person who owns 25% or more of each entity in the chain, plus at least one control person, with ID for each.
items.format: Signed certification in the form of the FinCEN CDD Rule (31 CFR 1010.230), supported by operating agreements and cap tables.
items.why: Concealed owners, sanctioned owners and nominee structures (0.3).
items.pass: Every 25%+ owner and a control person are named, identified and screened; ownership percentages tie to governing documents.
items.fail: Unidentified owners, bearer shares, trusts with undisclosed beneficiaries, or ownership that does not tie.
items.verify: Establish beneficial ownership through our own CDD (operating agreements, cap tables, certified charts); do not rely on CTA BOI filings, which US companies no longer make.

items.request: Detailed resume for each principal and senior team member: every employer, title, dates, degrees, licences (Series, CPA, bar), and board seats for the last 20 years.
items.format: Signed CV with month-level dates and contactable references for each role.
items.why: Resume inflation is a documented fraud precursor (Drive Planning, Toltec Capital, 0.2).
items.pass: Every employer, title, date, degree and licence is confirmed by the background-check firm or the issuing body.
items.fail: Any unverifiable or inflated title, degree, licence or date range.
items.verify: Background-check firm verifies employment and education directly; licences checked on FINRA BrokerCheck, IAPD and state boards.

items.request: Signed self-disclosure questionnaire for the sponsor and each principal covering criminal matters, civil litigation, bankruptcies, judgments, liens, regulatory actions (SEC, FINRA, state), terminations and investigations in the last 10 years.
items.format: Signed and dated questionnaire under penalty of rescission, with supporting documents for each disclosed item.
items.why: 21% of managers misrepresented past legal or regulatory problems; 10% would have passed as clean on self-disclosure alone (0.2).
items.pass: Every matter found by the independent background check was disclosed in the questionnaire.
items.fail: Any material matter found independently that was not disclosed, or a partial disclosure ('strategic misstatement').
items.verify: Reconcile item by item to the independent background check and Form ADV; record any refused question as a tracked field.

items.request: Track-record summary listing every deal, fund and vehicle the sponsor and each principal has ever managed or led, including closed, abandoned and written-off ones, with amount invested, dates, realized and unrealized value, gross and net returns.
items.format: Excel schedule, one row per deal or vehicle, with the principal who led each.
items.why: Cherry-picked records, survivorship and backfill bias (0.13).
items.pass: Schedule is complete: it reconciles to Form ADV, prior offering documents, public filings and references; no vehicle we find elsewhere is missing.
items.fail: Omitted vehicles, returns shown only gross, compounded IRRs, or a record borrowed from people not primarily responsible.
items.verify: Cross-check against Form ADV, SEC filings, press, prior LP references and state records; recompute from cash flows at confirmatory stage.

items.request: Statement of the sponsor's deal pace and capacity: deals per year and AUM for each of the last 5 years against investment and operating headcount, and the annual deployment target against the size of the market it invests in.
items.format: Table by year with headcount by function.
items.why: Rapid growth in deal volume without the operating bench is associated with worse outcomes; deployment pressure undermines selective underwriting (0.2, 0.10).
items.pass: Team size grew in step with deal pace and AUM; deployment target is a small share of the target market.
items.fail: Deal pace or AUM doubling without a matching increase in senior team; deployment target a large share of the market.
items.verify: Check headcount against LinkedIn and Form ADV Part 1 employee counts; deal counts against public records.

items.request: Deal-sourcing statement: how the deal came to the sponsor, whether it is claimed to be proprietary, who else saw it, and whether a banker or broker ran a process.
items.format: Written statement naming the intermediary, if any, and the other bidders or investors approached.
items.why: Unverified 'proprietary deal' claims; a sponsor that claims to close far more than about 6 of 100 opportunities is not screening (0.1).
items.pass: Claim corroborated by the intermediary or seller; sponsor's stated close rate is consistent with institutional funnels.
items.fail: 'Proprietary' claim no one can corroborate; implausibly high close rate.
items.verify: Ask the seller, banker or broker directly who else saw the deal.

items.request: List of every other investor, lender and co-investor in the deal and the lead investor, with amounts, and written consent for us to contact each about the diligence it performed.
items.format: Table with contact names; consent letter.
items.why: Social proof substitutes for diligence ('X and Y are already in') (0.4, 0.12).
items.pass: We confirm directly with each named investor that it is in and what diligence it performed.
items.fail: Named investors who deny or downplay involvement, or sponsor refuses consent to contact.
items.verify: Call each investor on an independently obtained number.

items.request: Lead investor's diligence-intensity record: hours spent with management in person, sites visited, reference calls made, and what was skipped for timing.
items.format: Written statement from the lead (not the sponsor), with dates.
items.why: Diligence thins in hot markets and widens the spread of outcomes (Fu and Taylor, 0.1); VC norm is about 118 hours and about 10 reference calls per deal.
items.pass: Lead states hours, sites and references; reference calls at or above about 10 (13 late-stage, 8 early-stage).
items.fail: Lead cannot state hours, sites and references, or relies on another investor's work.
items.verify: Confirm with the lead directly; record in our diligence-intensity field.

items.request: Market and cycle statement: where the asset class is in the credit cycle, who bought recent comparables and how they were financed, new supply coming (issuance, construction, unlocks, queued capacity), and recent thematic vehicle launches in the same theme.
items.format: Written memo with data sources (comps list with buyer type and financing source; supply pipeline).
items.why: Cheap credit lets a small levered minority set prices; diligence thins at the top (0.10).
items.pass: Statement addresses each line of the 0.10 cycle scorecard with sources; if 3 or more bubble features are present, it names the exit buyer and multiple once supply arrives.
items.fail: Deck cites the round's price, a marquee co-investor or a national demand forecast as validation in an asset class scoring late-cycle on 3 or more lines.
items.verify: We score the 0.10 scorecard ourselves from BIS, Fed Z.1, REIT-implied caps, fund-launch counts and the comps' financing.

items.request: Statement of every law, regulation, exemption, licence, tax credit or agency decision the deal relies on, with its current status and the sponsor's description of it.
items.format: Written schedule with citations, reviewed by sponsor counsel.
items.why: Decks describe rules that have changed (for example 'cannabis is now Schedule III' is wrong for adult-use) (0.18, A.3 item 29).
items.pass: Each line is current as of November 2026 per the 0.18 status table and will be re-checked at signing.
items.fail: Any reliance on a vacated, postponed or misdescribed rule (SEC Private Fund Adviser rules, IA AML rule, CTA BOI, 506(c) relief, cannabis scheduling, IRA credits).
items.verify: Our counsel checks each line against the primary source at signing.

items.request: Plain-language glossary: every term of art in the deck and model ('adjusted EBITDA', 'synthetic', 'visibility', 'hedge', 'compute', 'distribution rate') restated in one sentence with a number attached.
items.format: Written glossary annex.
items.why: Opaque jargon lets committees approve what they do not understand (London Whale, 0.12).
items.pass: Every key term is restated in one plain sentence with a number that ties to the model.
items.fail: Any key term the sponsor cannot restate with a number.
items.verify: IC members test each definition against the model; items no one in the approval chain can restate are not approved.

items.request: Timeline to signing, funding and close, with any deadline imposed by the seller, the lead or another investor and the reason for it.
items.format: Written timeline.
items.why: Seller-imposed deadlines are used to cut the diligence floor (0.1).
items.pass: Timeline accommodates the full diligence floor (site visits, in-person management hours, reference calls, third-party reports).
items.fail: Deadline that leaves no time for third-party reports or direct confirmations; pressure to act fast.
items.verify: We set the diligence floor in writing before the timeline is agreed and do not shrink it for competition.

items.request: Provide a schedule of every state and local license and registration held: license number, type (medical, adult-use, cultivation, processing, distribution, retail), licensee legal name, premises, expiry and status.
items.format: Schedule plus copies of each license.
items.why: License not real, current, in good standing or held by the operating entity.
items.pass: Every license confirmed by the regulator as current and in good standing, in the name of the operating entity.
items.fail: License in a different name, expired, suspended or unverifiable.
items.verify: Confirm each license directly with the state regulator's database and staff.

items.request: Provide the financial model's federal tax build, with a version rebuilt at full 280E on every dollar of revenue.
items.format: Native model with tax tab.
items.why: 280E understated in projections.
items.pass: Base case taxes at full 280E: only IRC 471 direct COGS deducted; operating expenses not deducted.
items.fail: Model deducts normal opex federally.
items.verify: We rebuild the tax ourselves.

items.request: Provide 3 to 5 years of annual financial statements plus TTM, audited or reviewed where available.
items.format: Audited or reviewed statements with accountant's reports; TTM management accounts.
items.why: Cash-basis or unreviewed books.
items.pass: Accrual-basis statements; audited or reviewed for at least the last fiscal year, or QoE converts to accrual.
items.fail: Cash-basis books, no audited or reviewed financials, inconsistent close.
items.verify: Call the auditor; tie to tax returns.

items.request: Provide revenue split by license type (medical under a qualifying state medical license vs adult-use) and by state, for 3 years and TTM.
items.format: POS and seed-to-sale reports tied to the GL.
items.why: Schedule III relief assumed for adult-use revenue.
items.pass: Split reconciles to POS and seed-to-sale data; adult-use modeled at full 280E.
items.fail: No split, or split that does not tie.
items.verify: Pull POS and tracking reports directly.

items.request: Provide the sell-side QoE report, its engagement letter and its scope section, if one exists.
items.format: Full report and engagement letter including procedures not performed.
items.why: A QoE carries no assurance; scope decides what was tested.
items.pass: Engagement type stated (SSAE 19 AUP or CS 100); procedures not performed listed; proof of cash covered every account in the bank confirmations.
items.fail: No engagement letter; proof of cash on a subset of accounts.
items.verify: Read the letter; confirm account list against bank confirmations.

items.request: Provide a 3-year EBITDA bridge from reported net income to reported EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and pro forma EBITDA, with an add-back schedule and support for every adjustment.
items.format: Spreadsheet with each adjustment, amount by year and supporting documents.
items.why: Buying inflated EBITDA ($8M marketed becoming $7M changes debt and price; claims at the deal multiple).
items.pass: Every add-back independently validated; validated adjusted EBITDA within the range used for price.
items.fail: Adjusted EBITDA with no bridge; unsupported add-backs.
items.verify: Buy-side QoE validates each adjustment.

items.request: Provide the banking relationships: bank name, account types, tenure, any account-closure history, and the cash-management process (vaults, armored transport, deposits).
items.format: Bank letters, statements and cash-handling SOPs.
items.why: Sudden de-banking.
items.pass: Established depository with multi-year tenure, no closure history and a documented cash-handling process.
items.fail: One bank, short tenure, prior closures.
items.verify: Confirm with the bank directly.

items.request: Provide the last three years of budgets with actuals for the same periods.
items.format: Board-approved budgets and actuals.
items.why: Optimistic misses are a fraud precursor (about a quarter of AAER misstatements began as optimistic errors).
items.pass: Misses not consistently optimistic; variances explained.
items.fail: Pattern of optimistic misses.
items.verify: Tie budgets to board minutes.

items.request: Provide the exit thesis naming buyers legally permitted to own the asset and the comparables used.
items.format: Memo with buyer list and comps.
items.why: Exit valued at consumer-staples multiples.
items.pass: Buyers permitted to own the asset under federal-illegality constraints on US-listed acquirers, banks and exchanges; comps discounted from consumer staples.
items.fail: Comps from staples or alcohol with no discount.
items.verify: Test buyer list against listing and lending constraints.

items.request: Provide management's forecast with its scenario ranges.
items.format: Native model.
items.why: Forecasts padded; ranges too narrow.
items.pass: We can apply a 20% haircut and widen ranges about 2x.
items.fail: Forecast with no ranges.
items.verify: Our base case haircuts 20%.

items.request: Provide the process description: banker, list of parties contacted, timetable and any seller-imposed deadline.
items.format: Process letter and timetable.
items.why: Auction fever and deadline-driven diligence cuts.
items.pass: Timetable allows full diligence (LMM benchmark 60 to 90 days LOI to close, WEAK) and a cooling-off period before final bid.
items.fail: Deadline used to cut diligence scope.
items.verify: Ask the banker directly; confirm with other bidders where possible.

items.request: Provide the walk-away price, the conservative cash flows behind it, the date it was set and who set it.
items.format: Dated memo.
items.why: Diligence run to confirm an answer already chosen.
items.pass: Walk-away price set before bidding by someone outside the deal team.
items.fail: No walk-away price; set by the deal champion.
items.verify: Check memo date against bid dates.

items.request: Draft term sheet or LOI with economics, security, conditions precedent, information and audit rights, consent rights, and exclusivity period.
items.format: Marked draft in Word.
items.why: Rights not negotiated before signing are not available later; LPs and minority investors rarely win in court (0.16).
items.pass: Term sheet includes information rights, audited financials, inspection and audit rights, and conditions precedent tied to the gating items in this packet.
items.fail: No information or audit rights; no conditions precedent for third-party reports; exclusivity without diligence access.
items.verify: Our counsel marks up against the gating items list.

items.request: Signed consent and authorization for independent background checks (criminal, civil, bankruptcy, regulatory, credit, media) on the sponsor, every principal, the CFO, controller, wire releaser and every placement agent or salesperson.
items.format: FCRA-compliant consent forms signed by each individual.
items.why: Fraud is usually collusive; second-tier executives and sales agents are defendants in placement frauds (Drive Planning, 0.2).
items.pass: Consents received for every named person in the chain, including the placement chain.
items.fail: Any principal, finance officer, wire releaser or placement agent refuses consent.
items.verify: Background-check firm confirms receipt and validity of every consent.

items.request: Signed authorization letters allowing us and our QoE provider to obtain statements and confirmations directly and unsolicited from every bank, custodian, administrator, auditor, prime broker, servicer and payment processor.
items.format: Signed letters addressed to each institution, on its own form where required.
items.why: Statements produced by the manager rather than a third party are the Ponzi enabler (0.4, 0.5).
items.pass: Authorization covers every institution that holds cash, assets or records for the sponsor and the deal.
items.fail: Refusal to authorize direct contact with any administrator, auditor, custodian, prime broker or bank.
items.verify: Send requests ourselves to contact details obtained independently, not from the sponsor.

items.request: Fully diluted capitalization table (all classes, options, RSUs, warrants, SAFEs, convertibles, benefit-fund issuance) and a list of every investor veto or consent right over financings and M&A.
items.format: Excel cap table reconciled to the stock ledger and charter; schedule of veto rights with document references.
items.why: Headline valuations use basic share counts; strategic investors with financing vetoes block rescue capital (0.6, 0.16).
items.pass: Cap table ties to the stock ledger, charter and option plan; price per share uses the fully diluted count; vetoes listed.
items.fail: Unreconciled cap table; omitted SAFEs or warrants; undisclosed strategic investor financing veto.
items.verify: Reconcile to charter filings, board minutes and transfer-agent or ledger records.

items.request: Statement of the sponsor's own capital at risk in this deal, the main fund's participation and pro rata, and why the deal is being syndicated to us.
items.format: Written statement with commitment amounts and source of the sponsor's cash.
items.why: Co-investments and side vehicles underperform the sponsoring GP's main fund on average (adverse selection) (0.13).
items.pass: Main fund takes its full pro rata and the sponsor has material capital at risk on the same terms as us.
items.fail: Main fund under-allocates, sponsor has no money at risk, or syndication exists to offload a deal the main fund will not hold.
items.verify: Confirm the main fund's allocation from the fund's administrator or capital-call notices.

items.request: Schedule of every fee, expense reimbursement and economic interest the sponsor and affiliates will receive (acquisition, asset management, monitoring, transaction, director, financing, disposition fees, carry or promote), and how fees offset.
items.format: Fee schedule with formulas and illustrative dollar amounts at base and downside cases.
items.why: Fee overcharging and missed offsets are recurring SEC findings (TZP Management, 0.15).
items.pass: All fees disclosed with formulas; offsets computed; sponsor economics reconcile to the model.
items.fail: Undisclosed fees, fees on committed rather than invested capital after the investment period, or no offset of portfolio-company fees.
items.verify: Recompute fee offsets from portfolio-company payments.

items.request: Distribution policy and any stated distribution rate or yield, with the cash source of each projected distribution.
items.format: Written policy and model tab mapping each distribution to an operating cash flow line.
items.why: A fixed distribution rate on an illiquid asset paid from new capital is the Ponzi signature (GPB Capital, Heller ATMs, 0.4).
items.pass: Every projected distribution is funded from asset-level operating cash flow in the model; no fixed or guaranteed rate.
items.fail: Guaranteed or fixed above-market returns; distributions funded by new capital, borrowing or return of capital described as yield.
items.verify: After funding, reconcile every distribution to its source account (monitoring item).

items.request: Proposed information and reporting package: quarterly financial statements and fee and performance statements, annual audit by a named auditor, valuation reports, covenant certificates, and notice obligations.
items.format: Draft reporting covenant or side-letter language; ILPA Reporting Template for funds.
items.why: No federal rule requires quarterly statements, fund audits or GP-led fairness opinions since the SEC Private Fund Adviser rules were vacated on June 5, 2024 (0.16, 0.18).
items.pass: Quarterly statements, an annual audit by a named auditor, and notice of material events are contractual obligations with fixed delivery deadlines.
items.fail: Reporting left to sponsor discretion; no audit requirement; no fee and expense disclosure.
items.verify: Our counsel confirms the obligations are in the operative documents, not only in the deck.

items.request: Organization chart of the sponsor and target finance and operations functions naming the CFO, controller, the person who releases wires, the person who reconciles accounts, and the person who reports to investors.
items.format: Chart with names, titles, reporting lines and tenure.
items.why: One person deciding, moving cash and reporting is the most consistent precursor to fraud; a 'CFO' who is really a controller is a gap (0.2, 0.4).
items.pass: Decision, cash movement and reporting sit with different people and an independent third party; titles match the work done.
items.fail: Same person decides, releases wires and reports; no CFO able to give an independent view; long-tenured closed inner circle controlling reporting and cash.
items.verify: Compare with the bank or administrator signatory list and with interviews of staff below the principals.

items.request: Sponsor's walk-away price or maximum leverage and the conservative cash-flow case it is based on, set before bidding.
items.format: Written note with the conservative case attached.
items.why: Diligence run to confirm an answer already chosen is the most common M&A process failure (0.1, 0.12).
items.pass: Walk-away price is set from conservative cash flows by people separate from the deal champions.
items.fail: No walk-away price, or the deal champion also runs the valuation.
items.verify: Our own valuation team sets our walk-away independently of the deal team.

items.request: If any 280E relief or Schedule III treatment is claimed: provide the DEA registration obtained under the expedited pathway for state medical licensees.
items.format: Registration certificate and DEA correspondence.
items.why: Relief claimed without registration.
items.pass: Registration exists, is current and covers the medical activity claimed.
items.fail: No registration, or registration pending.
items.verify: Confirm with DEA.

items.request: Provide the LOI with valuation basis, financing sources and conditions.
items.format: Executed or draft LOI with sources and uses.
items.why: Retrade risk: valuation and financing not qualified before the LOI.
items.pass: Valuation stated on validated (not marketed) EBITDA; financing sources named with indicative terms before signing.
items.fail: LOI priced on unvalidated adjusted EBITDA or with no identified financing.
items.verify: Confirm lender interest directly with named lenders.

items.request: If any relief is claimed: provide a written tax opinion on 280E treatment after the partial rule.
items.format: Signed opinion with stated assumptions.
items.why: Relief resting on a deck statement.
items.pass: Opinion from named independent counsel covering the activity, the apportionment and the absence of IRS guidance.
items.fail: No opinion, or opinion from a marketing source.
items.verify: Our tax counsel reviews.

items.request: If the operator holds both medical and adult-use licenses: provide the apportionment method allocating COGS, revenue and overhead between medical and adult-use.
items.format: Written method with workpapers.
items.why: Apportionment that would not survive audit.
items.pass: Method allocates COGS, revenue and overhead on documented drivers; our tax advisor concludes it would survive audit.
items.fail: No apportionment method.
items.verify: Re-perform on a sample month.

items.request: Provide the base case: margins flat at current (plus only named, costed drivers), management forecast haircut about 20%, exit multiple equal to or below entry.
items.format: Model tab with the haircut and exit assumption shown explicitly.
items.why: Committee asked to approve a hope.
items.pass: Base case clears the hurdle (target gross IRR about 22%, range 20% to 25%; MOIC about 2.5x).
items.fail: Base case below hurdle, or base case uses multiple expansion or unnamed margin expansion.
items.verify: Rebuild independently and compare.

items.request: Provide the downside case at full 280E treatment on all revenue, including medical.
items.format: Model tab.
items.why: Relief that never arrives (litigation, no IRS guidance).
items.pass: Deal still works at full 280E; relief shown only as upside.
items.fail: Deal fails at full 280E.
items.verify: Rebuild.

items.request: Provide the attribution test: the return recomputed with margins flat and exit equal to entry, and the share of the sponsor-case return that survives.
items.format: Model tab and one-line summary.
items.why: Returns driven mostly by multiple expansion (about 80% of search-fund exit value).
items.pass: Attribution test still clears the hurdle; share surviving reported.
items.fail: Most of the sponsor-case return disappears.
items.verify: Recompute ourselves (red-team step).

items.request: Confirm that no prior-year 280E refund claims are counted in value, liquidity or working capital.
items.format: Officer's statement and schedule of any filed claims.
items.why: Refund claims booked as an asset.
items.pass: Zero value assigned to refund claims.
items.fail: Refunds counted.
items.verify: Review balance sheet and model.

items.request: Provide the downside case: margins flat or lower, exit at entry minus 1 to 2 turns, revenue from base rates, management ranges widened about 2x, a secular-decline case where relevant, and an extended hold if a CEO change is likely.
items.format: Model tab with assumptions listed.
items.why: Sponsor scenario tabs understate risk (Toys 'R' Us).
items.pass: Debt serviced and equity not wiped out, or the loss is explicitly accepted by IC in writing.
items.fail: Downside not built, or copied from the sponsor's scenario tab.
items.verify: Build our own downside from base rates.

items.request: Provide a base case holding margins flat, with the state's pricing trend.
items.format: Model and wholesale/retail price history by state.
items.why: Margin expansion in a price-compressing market.
items.pass: Margins flat or lower in base case.
items.fail: Margin expansion assumed.
items.verify: Compare to state price data.

items.request: Provide the return attribution split: revenue growth, margin change, debt paydown, multiple change and recap or dividend proceeds.
items.format: Table in the IC memo tied to the model.
items.why: Recap-driven IRR presented as earnings growth.
items.pass: All five components shown and summing to the total return.
items.fail: Components not separable, or recap proceeds blended into growth.
items.verify: Recompute from the model.

items.request: Provide the valuation with a discount to consumer-staples comps for the restricted buyer and lender pool.
items.format: Valuation memo.
items.why: Exit multiple borrowed from staples.
items.pass: Explicit discount applied and justified.
items.fail: No discount.
items.verify: Our own comps.

items.request: Provide the synergy table: cost synergies separate from revenue synergies, each with probability and timing, plus a dis-synergy line for lost customers and talent.
items.format: Table with owner and assumption per line.
items.why: Overpaying for unweighted synergies (Tyson-Hillshire; premium-driven write-downs).
items.pass: Every line probability-weighted; cost synergies timed 1 to 2 years, revenue 2 to 3+ years; dis-synergies included.
items.fail: Unweighted synergies or no dis-synergy line.
items.verify: Test each line with operators and customers.

items.request: Provide the change-of-control approval requirements and timeline for each licensed entity.
items.format: Counsel memo citing state rules.
items.why: Deal cannot close or license lost on transfer.
items.pass: Approval path and timeline known; closing conditioned on approvals.
items.fail: Transfer not permitted or unknown.
items.verify: Confirm with regulators.

items.request: Provide any option or abandonment-value analysis used to support price, with explicit ranged assumptions.
items.format: Model tab.
items.why: Pure DCF underbids, but option value can also rationalize a price.
items.pass: Assumptions explicit and ranged; price stays at or below walk-away.
items.fail: Option value used to justify a price above walk-away.
items.verify: Review assumptions against the walk-away memo.

items.request: Provide the value-creation plan with the share of value from each lever: revenue growth, incentives, add-ons, exit, governance, buying cheap, cost reduction.
items.format: Plan document with quantified levers.
items.why: Plans leaning on industry's weaker levers.
items.pass: Plan led by revenue growth and incentives; cost cuts and multiple arbitrage not the majority of value.
items.fail: Mostly cost cuts and multiple expansion.
items.verify: Compare with sponsor survey lever ratings (cost reduction important pre-deal in 36%).

items.request: Provide the exit analysis: buyer universe by route (strategic, financial, IPO) and the exit multiple basis.
items.format: Memo naming likely buyers.
items.why: IPO-dependent exits (IPO under 20% of exits).
items.pass: Exit achievable by strategic or financial buyer; exit multiple at or below entry.
items.fail: Exit depends on an IPO or on multiple expansion.
items.verify: Compare with exit-route base rates (about 50/30/under 20).

items.request: Provide debt commitment papers and term sheets.
items.format: Signed commitment letters with conditions.
items.why: Financing failure or off-market terms.
items.pass: Committed financing matches the LBO model's sources, pricing and covenants.
items.fail: Uncommitted financing or conditions outside buyer control.
items.verify: Confirm directly with lenders.

items.request: Provide every sponsor and affiliate fee agreement charged to the target (transaction, monitoring, director, exit fees) and the LPA fee-offset terms.
items.format: Executed agreements and LPA excerpts.
items.why: Monitoring-fee acceleration on exit (SEC fines 2015-2016).
items.pass: Monitoring fees within 1% to 5% of EBITDA, offset to LPs (typically 80/20); no acceleration on exit.
items.fail: Acceleration on exit; undisclosed fees.
items.verify: Read agreements and LPA directly.

items.request: Provide the management incentive plan, equity rollover terms and proposed board composition.
items.format: Term sheets and plan summary.
items.why: Misaligned incentives and weak governance.
items.pass: Management and employees near 17% of equity (CEO about 8%; 15% and 6% at larger firms); board 5 to 7 members with 1 to 2 outsiders.
items.fail: No incentive plan, or no outside directors.
items.verify: Compare with Gompers et al. benchmarks.

items.request: Provide the R&W insurance proposal or binder with draft exclusions, limit, retention and premium.
items.format: Broker proposal and draft policy.
items.why: Assuming coverage for known issues.
items.pass: Limit 10% to 20% of deal value; retention about 1%; premium about 2% to 3% of limit; every exclusion mapped to a diligence finding.
items.fail: Exclusions on financial-statement, material-contract or compliance reps, unmapped.
items.verify: Our broker reviews exclusions against diligence reports.

items.request: Provide the proposed indemnity package: survival period, basket, cap, escrow or holdback and specific indemnities.
items.format: Term sheet or SPA draft.
items.why: Survival too short (51% of claims arrive after 12 months, 24% after 24).
items.pass: Key reps survive at least 24 months where reps survive; basket 0.5% to 1% deductible; PPA escrow about 1%; uninsured cap near 10% of deal value; specific indemnity for every known issue.
items.fail: 12-month survival on key reps; no specific indemnities.
items.verify: Compare with ABA 2025 and SRS 2025 market data.

items.request: Provide earnout terms: metric definitions with worked examples, efforts standard or fixed spend, reporting and audit rights, cost allocation, staffing and working-capital rules, acceleration triggers, expert-not-arbitrator scope and record-keeping.
items.format: Draft earnout provisions.
items.why: Earnout disputes (Fortis v. J&J).
items.pass: Every checklist item present; efforts definition applies to every milestone, not only the first.
items.fail: Vague metrics, or efforts calibrated only to the first payment.
items.verify: Counsel review against the 5.11 checklist.

items.request: Where customer relationships are personal to the selling owner: provide seller-note or earnout terms tied to customer retention.
items.format: Draft seller note or earnout provisions with retention metric.
items.why: Owner-held relationships leave with the seller.
items.pass: Deferred consideration of a meaningful share of price conditioned on retention of named customers over at least 24 months.
items.fail: All consideration paid at close despite owner-dependent customers.
items.verify: Customer calls confirm who holds the relationship.

items.request: Track record as dated LP-level (or deal-level) cash flows for every fund, vehicle and deal ever managed, including closed and abandoned ones, so we can recompute returns ourselves.
items.format: Excel cash-flow ledger (dates, contributions, distributions, residual NAV) tied to capital-account statements from the administrator.
items.why: A track record is the sponsor's own exhibit; compounded IRRs, gross-only and selective periods are SEC exam findings (0.13).
items.pass: We recompute gross and net IRR, TVPI, DPI and a PME (KS-PME) from the cash flows and they match the sponsor's reported figures, with every difference explained in writing; shown with and without the top 1 or 2 outcomes.
items.fail: Returns we cannot recompute; IRRs compounded or compared with a time-weighted index; record collapses without the top 1 or 2 outcomes in a 'consistent singles' thesis.
items.verify: Obtain capital-account statements from the administrator directly and confirm with two or more prior LPs.

items.request: Deal-by-deal attribution: for each realized deal, the partners who sourced, led and managed it, whether each is still with the sponsor and in what role.
items.format: Table per deal with names and current status.
items.why: Reputation and skill sit with partners; records borrowed from people who have left are an SEC finding (0.13).
items.pass: Partners responsible for the majority of realized value are still at the sponsor and will lead this deal.
items.fail: Track record attributed to departed people, or this deal led by someone with no record.
items.verify: Confirm with references, former partners and LinkedIn histories.

items.request: Return decomposition for every realized deal: revenue and EBITDA growth, debt paydown and leverage, multiple change, and dividend recaps, as separate lines.
items.format: Excel bridge per deal from entry to exit equity value.
items.why: Returns from multiple expansion and financial engineering are not repeatable (0.7 item 6, 0.13).
items.pass: Operating improvement (earnings growth) explains the majority of realized value creation across the record.
items.fail: Record driven mainly by multiple expansion, leverage or recaps; decomposition refused.
items.verify: Recompute from entry and exit financials and purchase prices in deal documents.

items.request: Forecast record: every past projection, budget or investor guidance the sponsor or management gave for prior deals or years, alongside the actual result.
items.format: Table by deal or year, with the original projection documents attached.
items.why: Repeated optimistic misses are a fraud precursor (a quarter of SEC AAER misstatements began as optimistic errors); executive 80% ranges capture outcomes only 36% of the time (0.2, 0.6).
items.pass: Actuals land within the sponsor's stated ranges at a rate consistent with calibration and misses are not one-directional.
items.fail: A pattern of repeated optimistic misses, or past projections that cannot be produced.
items.verify: Compare with prior offering memoranda, lender reports and LP letters obtained from third parties.

items.request: Evidence of each claimed prior exit or founder success: filings, closing statements, cap tables and distribution records showing the outcome and the principal's role.
items.format: Third-party documents (SEC filings, closing statements, transfer-agent records).
items.why: Prior success is a material underwriting variable (founder success about 30% after a success vs 18% first-time) and is often inflated (0.2, 0.14).
items.pass: Every claimed exit is documented and the principal's stated role and proceeds are confirmed.
items.fail: Claimed exits that cannot be documented or where the principal's role was minor.
items.verify: Check SEC EDGAR, state filings and the acquirer's announcements; confirm with co-investors.

items.request: Reference list of at least 15 contactable people across former investors, lenders, co-investors, partners, former employees, customers and vendors, including people who left on bad terms.
items.format: Names, roles, relationship, dates and phone numbers; we add references we find independently.
items.why: Tips detect 43% of frauds, more than half from employees and almost a third from vendors and customers (0.2).
items.pass: We complete at least 10 reference calls (13 late-stage, 8 early-stage), at least half sourced by us, and ask each whether they were ever asked to do something with invoices, payments or records that felt wrong.
items.fail: Only friendly references offered; references who decline or describe pressure on records, payments or invoices.
items.verify: Source independent references from prior deal documents, LinkedIn, litigation dockets and former employers.

items.request: Last 8 quarterly investor letters or portfolio commentaries (or lender reports for operating companies).
items.format: Letters as sent, with dates.
items.why: Material changes in disclosure language predict worse outcomes; early letters that dwell on refinancing and capital structure predict weaker returns (0.4, 0.13).
items.pass: Every material change in risk, legal or financial language between letters is explained in writing.
items.fail: Unexplained edits to risk or legal language; commentary dwelling on refinancing, covenants or capital structure.
items.verify: Text-diff the letters ourselves and send written questions for each material edit.

items.request: Leadership assessment for the CEO and top team against the plan: can the incumbent execute it, how gaps close, named internal and external successors, and how requirements change across the hold.
items.format: Written assessment by the sponsor plus successor bench list.
items.why: 69% of buyouts change CEO during the hold; team is the top factor in both successes and failures (0.14).
items.pass: Each of the four entry questions is answered with evidence; a named successor exists for the CEO and CFO; the downside case budgets a CEO change.
items.fail: No successor; plan depends on a single person; no budget for a leadership change.
items.verify: Our own management interviews, references and, for control deals, an independent leadership assessment.

items.request: Finance-function evidence: named CFO and controller with CVs, accounting policies (including revenue recognition), month-end close calendar, internal-audit or equivalent function, and an employee census reconciled to payroll.
items.format: CVs, policy manual, close checklist, census and payroll register for the same date.
items.why: FTX had no accounting department and no complete employee list; missing accounting function is an automatic pass (0.4).
items.pass: In-house CFO or controller exists, census reconciles to payroll headcount and cost, and revenue recognition is documented.
items.fail: No accounting function, census does not reconcile to payroll, or 'CFO' is a bookkeeper or controller.
items.verify: Reconcile census to payroll provider reports obtained directly; interview the controller without the principal.

items.request: Board and voting-control map: every director with domain expertise, independence and committee roles; voting control by class including any super-voting shares and their sunset; audit committee composition.
items.format: Charter, voting agreements, board list with bios.
items.why: Theranos: 100-to-1 founder votes and a board with no medical or financial expertise (0.2, 0.14).
items.pass: At least one independent director able to chair audit; directors with domain expertise; any founder super-voting control has a sunset and is priced.
items.fail: Founder super-voting control without sunset plus no audit committee; celebrity board without domain experts.
items.verify: Confirm from charter filings and director interviews.

items.request: Management and employee equity schedule, vesting terms and incentive plans.
items.format: Option plan, grant ledger, vesting schedules.
items.why: Misaligned incentives; PE norm is management 17% of equity (CEO 8%) (0.14).
items.pass: Management equity and vesting are material and aligned with the plan horizon, benchmarked against 17% management / 8% CEO.
items.fail: No management equity or fully vested at close.
items.verify: Reconcile to the cap table and option ledger.

items.request: Lead investor or sponsor monitoring capacity: board seats held per partner, travel distance to the company, and partner time committed.
items.format: Table of the deal partner's current board seats and portfolio load.
items.why: Monitoring intensity improves outcomes (Bernstein, Giroud and Townsend, 0.14).
items.pass: Lead partner has bandwidth (board load and proximity) to monitor actively.
items.fail: Overloaded partner or no board seat.
items.verify: Confirm board seats from company filings.

items.request: For family or founder companies: independent board composition, CFO, and the outside experience of next-generation family members holding or taking board seats.
items.format: Board list with bios; family member CVs.
items.why: Family companies without independent oversight hide governance failures (0.14).
items.pass: Independent director able to chair audit; a real CFO; next-generation directors with outside experience (practitioner guide 7 to 10 years and a C-level role).
items.fail: Board wholly family-controlled with no independent director; next generation with no outside experience.
items.verify: Interview directors and verify CVs.

items.request: In-person access: a schedule of site visits to every material location and in-person sessions with management (not only the principal), sized to meet our written diligence floor.
items.format: Agreed calendar with attendees.
items.why: Refusal of on-site diligence is a universal red flag; thinner diligence widens the spread of outcomes (0.1, 0.4).
items.pass: Diligence floor met: every material site visited and in-person management hours logged; any shortfall recorded in the memo.
items.fail: Refusal of site visits or of access to staff below the principal.
items.verify: We log hours, sites and references in the diligence-intensity field (0.7 item 7).

items.request: Written answers, signed by an officer, to every question in our hints log (each data-room reference to lost customers, cancellation letters, volume declines, auditor changes, disputes or irregularities).
items.format: Signed Q&A log with dates and the identity of the answering officer.
items.why: Paragon Metals: the buyer saw hints but never asked the prepared questions and lost years in litigation (0.16).
items.pass: Every hint has a written question, an answer, the asker and the date; the model is re-run for any answer that changes a number.
items.fail: Unanswered or deflected questions; verbal answers that differ from documents.
items.verify: Confirm answers with the third party involved (customer, auditor, lender); track refused or deflected questions as a reported field.

items.request: Complete list of every investor, beneficial owner, borrower, guarantor, key customer, supplier, agent and counterparty in the deal chain, with full legal names, dates of birth or registration numbers, nationality and addresses, for sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening.
items.format: Excel list in screening-ready format.
items.why: Sanctioned persons hidden in ownership chains; OFAC 50 Percent Rule blocks entities owned 50% or more by blocked persons even if unlisted (0.3).
items.pass: No match on OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, UN, EU and UK lists; no entity owned 50% or more in aggregate by blocked persons; PEPs identified and escalated; adverse media reviewed and cleared.
items.fail: Confirmed sanctions match or 50%-rule block; unexplained PEP exposure; unresolved adverse media.
items.verify: Our screening vendor screens at onboarding and continuously; ownership chains traced for the 50% rule.

items.request: Source-of-funds evidence for the sponsor's and each principal's commitment to this deal: the specific accounts the money will come from and how it got there.
items.format: Bank or brokerage statements for 6 or more months showing the accumulation of the funds, plus documents for any large inflows.
items.why: Illicit or borrowed money presented as equity; a high 506(c) minimum shifts the burden to verifying the source of cash (0.3).
items.pass: Funds trace to documented, lawful sources and are not third-party financed unless disclosed.
items.fail: Untraceable inflows, funds from unrelated third parties, or financed equity presented as cash.
items.verify: Statements obtained directly from the institution; large inflows traced to source documents.

items.request: Source-of-wealth narrative for each principal and each 25%+ beneficial owner, with corroborating documents (sale agreements, tax returns, K-1s, inheritance or business records).
items.format: Written narrative plus documents covering how total net worth was accumulated.
items.why: Source of funds and source of wealth are different; a single bank statement is not a source-of-wealth narrative (0.3).
items.pass: Narrative is plausible against career history and corroborated by third-party documents for the main components of wealth.
items.fail: Wealth inconsistent with documented career; uncorroborated narrative; reliance on a single statement.
items.verify: Corroborate against tax transcripts, public records and the background check.

items.request: Sponsor's AML and sanctions compliance policy, the name of whoever performs KYC on the sponsor's other investors (GP or administrator), and whether that party files SARs.
items.format: Policy documents, administrator services agreement, last independent AML test.
items.why: Investment advisers have no federal AML program or SAR obligation until Jan. 1, 2028; do not assume CIP or sanctions screening was run on other LPs (0.3, 0.18).
items.pass: A written AML and sanctions program exists, benchmarked to OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments (management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and auditing, training), with a named KYC owner.
items.fail: No AML program and no administrator KYC on co-investors.
items.verify: Confirm the KYC scope directly with the administrator.

items.request: Accredited-investor or qualified-purchaser verification evidence for every investor in a 506(c) offering (tax returns, W-2s, bank statements or a licensed professional's letter), or, under the minimum-investment route, proof that the minimum ($200,000 natural persons, $1,000,000 entities) was paid in cash, not third-party financed, with a written representation.
items.format: Verification file per investor; third-party verification letters dated within 90 days of the sale.
items.why: 506(c) requires reasonable steps to verify, not self-certification (17 CFR 230.506(c)(2)(ii)) (0.3).
items.pass: Every investor has documentary verification dated within 90 days, or satisfies all minimum-investment conditions with source-of-cash evidence.
items.fail: Self-certification only; stale letters; financed minimums.
items.verify: Sample investor files and confirm letters with the issuing professional.

items.request: Schedule of all litigation, arbitration, regulatory proceedings, subpoenas and threatened claims in the last 10 years involving the sponsor entity, each principal and the target, with pleadings and outcomes.
items.format: Schedule plus copies of complaints, settlements and judgments.
items.why: 41% of funds in the ODD sample had a past legal or regulatory problem, more than twice the rate in Form ADV (0.2).
items.pass: Schedule reconciles to our independent litigation searches in every relevant federal and state court; no undisclosed matters.
items.fail: Undisclosed matters found in our searches; pattern of investor or lender suits.
items.verify: Run docket searches (PACER, state courts) on the entity and every principal ourselves.

items.request: Internal investigations log for the last 3 years: every allegation, who investigated, findings and how each matter was closed.
items.format: Log with case summaries; board or audit committee minutes where matters were reported.
items.why: Misconduct runs about 64 times the most expansive public database; a clean public record is weak evidence (0.15).
items.pass: Log exists, matters were investigated independently of the accused, and closures are documented.
items.fail: No log; matters closed by the accused's chain of command; repeat issues.
items.verify: Interview the person who runs investigations and the audit committee chair.

items.request: Whistleblower hotline details (phone, e-mail, web) and 3 years of hotline statistics: volume, categories, anonymity rate and resolution times.
items.format: Hotline vendor report and policy.
items.why: One-fifth of hotlines tested were non-functional; tip-detected frauds run a median 17 months vs 24 (auditor) and 36 (law enforcement) (0.15).
items.pass: Hotline exists, is operated independently of management, and reports volume and resolution times for 3 years.
items.fail: No hotline, hotline routed to the CEO, or statistics unavailable.
items.verify: We test the hotline ourselves (third-party stage).

items.request: Compliance program documents: code of ethics, compliance manual, personal-trading and conflicts policies, gifts and entertainment, and the last annual compliance review.
items.format: Policies and the latest annual review signed by the CCO.
items.why: DOJ expects comprehensive pre-acquisition compliance diligence and post-close integration (0.15).
items.pass: Program covers the business's actual risks and has been reviewed in the last 12 months.
items.fail: No program or a template never adapted or tested.
items.verify: Test sample controls during diligence; plan a 100-day compliance integration and audit.

items.request: Multiemployer pension plan participation and estimated withdrawal liability, and the ownership structure relative to the 80% common-control threshold.
items.format: Plan notices, actuarial withdrawal-liability estimates, ownership chart.
items.why: Sun Capital funds were held liable for a portfolio company's withdrawal liability (0.15).
items.pass: Withdrawal liability is quantified and ownership is structured to avoid 80% common control where liability exists.
items.fail: Unquantified withdrawal liability; sponsor funds under common control.
items.verify: Request estimates directly from plan administrators.

items.request: Exit antitrust analysis for any strategic-exit thesis: overlapping products and the HSR position of likely acquirers.
items.format: Counsel memo.
items.why: Killer acquisitions cluster just below HSR thresholds; expect FTC and DOJ scrutiny of sub-threshold deals (0.15).
items.pass: The exit thesis survives antitrust review or names non-strategic buyers.
items.fail: Exit depends on a single strategic buyer facing antitrust risk.
items.verify: Our counsel's review.

items.request: Trailing 36 months of bank statements for every account of the sponsor's deal entities, the issuer and every operating or asset-owning entity, plus the bank confirmations used in any QoE.
items.format: Bank-issued PDFs or direct bank delivery; full statements with every page; list of accounts tied to the bank-confirmation responses.
items.why: Proof of cash catches revenue and distributions that exist only on the P&L (0.5).
items.pass: Deposits reconcile to reported revenue and outflows to reported expenses and distributions for every month; every account on the bank confirmations is in the set; no unexplained related-party transfers.
items.fail: Gaps in months or accounts, statements produced by the sponsor rather than the bank, or unreconciled differences.
items.verify: Obtain statements directly from each bank under signed authorization and compare with the sponsor's copies.

items.request: Authorized-signatory list and wire-approval matrix for every account, as confirmed by the bank or the administrator (not described by the sponsor).
items.format: Bank- or administrator-issued signatory cards and approval matrix.
items.why: 16% of managers described the wire-signature process differently from their administrator (0.5).
items.pass: The bank's or administrator's matrix matches the sponsor's description and requires at least two people, including one independent of the investment decision, to release funds.
items.fail: Single-signatory release, mismatch with the administrator, or refusal to let us obtain it directly.
items.verify: Obtain directly from the bank or administrator.

items.request: Average daily (or intra-quarter) balances of cash, debt and assets for the last 8 quarters, alongside period-end figures.
items.format: Schedule derived from bank and loan statements, with daily data available on request.
items.why: Repo 105 moved up to $50B off Lehman's balance sheet at quarter-ends (0.4).
items.pass: Period-end balances are consistent with intra-quarter averages; no recurring financing that unwinds just after period-end.
items.fail: Period-end cash materially above, or debt materially below, intra-quarter averages; recurring quarter-end transactions.
items.verify: Compute averages ourselves from daily bank and loan statements.

items.request: Bank account list with balances by institution and the insured share of each, plus every pooled cash vehicle (money market funds, cash-management products, sweeps, stablecoins, tokenized cash).
items.format: Schedule tied to bank statements; fund fact sheets and holdings for each pooled vehicle.
items.why: SVB had 94% uninsured deposits; the Reserve Primary Fund gated and paid 99 cents only after two years (0.11).
items.pass: Cash is spread across banks, or held in insured sweeps or Treasury MMFs; no loan covenant forces a single bank; pooled vehicles are looked through.
items.fail: Single uninsured bank; material cash in vehicles that can gate; covenant forcing a single bank.
items.verify: Confirm balances directly with each institution; look through MMF holdings.

items.request: Statement of how many weeks of payroll and debt service the business could meet if its main bank closed this morning, with the supporting cash map.
items.format: Short memo with calculation.
items.why: SVB-type failures threaten payroll (0.11).
items.pass: Cash outside the main bank or insured covers at least the payroll and debt service until a replacement bank is in place; plan documented.
items.fail: Payroll depends on uninsured balances at a single bank.
items.verify: Recompute from the bank account list.

items.request: Audited financial statements for the last 3 years for the sponsor's vehicles and the issuer, with the auditor's engagement letters, management letters, and the auditor's PCAOB registration or peer-review report.
items.format: Auditor-signed statements; engagement and management letters; latest peer review.
items.why: Madoff's auditor was a two-partner firm with no peer review; non-Big 4 auditor plus internal pricing is associated with misrepresentation (0.4).
items.pass: Unqualified opinions by an independent auditor sized to the mandate, with a clean peer review; management-letter points remediated.
items.fail: No audit, qualified opinion, undersized or unreviewed auditor, or a non-Big 4 auditor combined with internal pricing without justification.
items.verify: Call the audit partner directly on an independently obtained number; confirm the peer review with the AICPA or PCAOB.

items.request: History of auditor changes, resignations, late audits, restatements and any unbooked rebates or post-closing adjustments for the last 5 years, with explanations.
items.format: Schedule with resignation letters and restatement memos.
items.why: Frauds start small; a late audit, restated quarter or unbooked rebate is the early signal (0.4); Cloudbreak counterparties hid an auditor resignation (0.16).
items.pass: No unexplained auditor change, late audit or restatement.
items.fail: Auditor resignation, repeated late audits or restatements explained away.
items.verify: Ask the prior auditor directly why the relationship ended.

items.request: Reconciliation of adjusted EBITDA (or any non-GAAP metric) to GAAP, with support for every add-back.
items.format: Excel bridge with invoices, contracts or payroll evidence per add-back.
items.why: Adjusted earnings with no GAAP reconciliation is a classic sales-side tell; losses are claimed at the deal multiple (0.4, 0.16).
items.pass: Every add-back is documented, non-recurring and accepted by the QoE.
items.fail: Unsupported or recurring add-backs; no GAAP reconciliation.
items.verify: QoE tests each add-back.

items.request: Schedule of every SPV, joint venture, guarantee, keepwell, comfort letter and 'moral obligation' support given by the sponsor, issuer or affiliates.
items.format: Schedule plus the underlying agreements; officer certification of completeness.
items.why: Enron's partnerships and banks' SIVs held risk off the balance sheet with implied sponsor support (0.4).
items.pass: All off-balance-sheet support is disclosed and included in a consolidated look-through of leverage.
items.fail: Undisclosed guarantees or vehicles found in searches or footnotes.
items.verify: Reconcile to UCC, litigation and secretary-of-state searches and audit footnotes.

items.request: Every factoring, supply-chain-finance, receivables-sale, inventory-finance and similar agreement of the issuer and every affiliate and principal-owned entity, with current balances.
items.format: Executed agreements and statements from each provider.
items.why: First Brands: reported leverage about 5x, about 20x counting factoring and supply-chain finance (0.4, Spine).
items.pass: All such financing is disclosed, reconciles to provider statements and to what each lender is told, and is added to leverage.
items.fail: Undisclosed facilities; balances that differ from provider statements; financing through founder-owned entities.
items.verify: Confirm balances directly with each provider; compare with UCC search results.

items.request: Related-party transaction schedule: every transaction, lease, loan, service agreement or payment between the sponsor, principals, their families or entities and the deal entities, for the last 3 years.
items.format: Schedule plus agreements; officer certification.
items.why: Steering good deals to insiders; commingling; insider leakage (Momentum Advisors) (0.4, 0.15).
items.pass: All related-party flows are disclosed, at market terms, and approved by an independent party.
items.fail: Undisclosed related-party payments found in bank statements.
items.verify: Match against bank-statement counterparties.

items.request: Statements for every account the principals control that has received or sent money to or from the deal entities or investors, and a certification that no fund or investor money passes through personal accounts.
items.format: Bank statements and signed certification.
items.why: Commingling of personal and fund accounts is a universal red flag (0.4).
items.pass: No investor or entity money passes through personal accounts; all flows are documented.
items.fail: Any commingling.
items.verify: Trace inflows and outflows in the 36-month statements.

items.request: Evidence that customer or fund assets are held in accounts titled to the fund or customer at a custodian outside the sponsor's group, and a reconciliation of those assets to customer liabilities.
items.format: Custodian account-title documents and reconciliation.
items.why: Customer assets used for other ventures (FTX); omnibus accounts complicated Lehman's broker-dealer liquidation (0.4, 0.5).
items.pass: Assets are segregated in fund- or customer-titled accounts at an independent custodian and reconcile to liabilities.
items.fail: Assets in sponsor-titled or omnibus accounts, or not reconciled to liabilities.
items.verify: Confirm account title and balance directly with the custodian.

items.request: Distribution history: every distribution paid to investors in the last 5 years, with the source account and the underlying asset or portfolio cash flow that funded it.
items.format: Schedule tied to bank statements.
items.why: GPB Capital paid 'portfolio cash flow' distributions from new capital (0.4, 0.5).
items.pass: Every distribution traces to asset-level operating cash flow, not to new subscriptions or borrowing.
items.fail: Distributions funded by new investor money (the definition of a Ponzi) or by undisclosed borrowing.
items.verify: Trace each distribution in the bank statements.

items.request: For returns said to come from operating assets (ATMs, machines, locations, loans, leases): an asset register with serial numbers and locations, and revenue files from the processor, servicer or counterparty.
items.format: Asset register plus processor or servicer reports delivered directly to us.
items.why: Heller ATM scheme: fixed 'ATM fee' distributions funded by new money (0.4, 0.5).
items.pass: Sample assets exist on site inspection and processor revenue matches reported revenue.
items.fail: Assets that cannot be located; revenue only from sponsor reports.
items.verify: Obtain processor and servicer files directly; inspect a sample of assets.

items.request: Sales by customer for the top 10 customers for 3 years, with contracts, and permission to call each customer and obtain its volume forecast.
items.format: Customer-level revenue schedule tied to invoices and cash receipts.
items.why: Paragon Metals: the CEO hid volume cuts by the largest customers; supplier sales growth that outruns customers' purchases predicts revenue fraud (0.4, 0.16).
items.pass: Reported sales to each top customer are consistent with the customer's own purchase, inventory and payables trends; customer forecasts support the model.
items.fail: Gap between reported sales growth and customer purchase growth; jumps in customer inventory or payables (channel stuffing); refusal to allow customer calls.
items.verify: Call top customers directly; use filings or confirmations of public customers.

items.request: Assumption source log: for every key model input, the source document, who produced it, and whether it is a sponsor or management figure.
items.format: Table keyed to model input cells.
items.why: Anchoring: committees re-label the sponsor's figure as their own (0.12 bias question 7).
items.pass: Every key input has a source; sponsor figures are identified and independently tested.
items.fail: Inputs with no source.
items.verify: Trace a sample of inputs to source documents.

items.request: Management forecast alongside the sponsor's base case, with the haircut applied stated explicitly.
items.format: Model tab with both cases.
items.why: Median PE discount to management EBITDA forecasts is 20%; executive 80% ranges capture outcomes only 36% of the time (0.6, 0.7).
items.pass: Base case applies an explicit haircut of about 20% to management's forecast, or justifies a smaller one with the forecast record.
items.fail: Base case equals management's forecast.
items.verify: Compare with the forecast record.

items.request: Downside case built from base rates (the outcome distribution of a reference class of similar deals), with sponsor ranges widened about 2x.
items.format: Model tab with the reference class cited.
items.why: Management downside cases are midpoints, not floors (0.6, 0.12).
items.pass: Downside case uses an outside-view base rate and the deal still meets its minimum hurdle or covenant tests.
items.fail: Downside is the base case with a small haircut, or the deal fails at base-rate outcomes.
items.verify: We rebuild the downside ourselves.

items.request: Flat-margin base case, or a costed line-by-line bridge naming every efficiency that expands margins.
items.format: Model tab or cost bridge.
items.why: Margins do not expand with scale on average (6,103 IPO firms, 1975 to 2016) (0.6).
items.pass: Base case holds margins flat unless each efficiency is costed and evidenced.
items.fail: Margin expansion assumed from scale without a costed bridge.
items.verify: Test each efficiency with operations diligence.

items.request: Exit cases: exit multiple equal to or below entry; entry minus 1 to 2 turns; and exit equal to entry with margins flat.
items.format: Model scenarios with returns for each.
items.why: Search-fund value creation was about 80% multiple expansion; exit = entry is not conservative at a cyclical peak (0.6, 0.7).
items.pass: The deal clears its hurdle with exit equal to entry and margins flat, and shows the return at entry minus 1 to 2 turns.
items.fail: Return depends on multiple expansion.
items.verify: Recompute in our copy of the model.

items.request: Reverse valuation ('what must be true'): the steady-state margin, growth and exit multiple the price implies, on a fully diluted share count.
items.format: Model tab.
items.why: Adding RSUs and options moved one implied valuation from $1.25T to about $1.7T (0.6).
items.pass: Implied margin, growth and multiple are within the range achieved by peers and historical high-growth companies.
items.fail: Price requires outcomes no peer has achieved.
items.verify: Benchmark against peers ourselves.

items.request: Return attribution for this deal's base case: earnings growth, debt paydown, multiple change and any dividend recap, as separate lines.
items.format: Model bridge.
items.why: A memo that cannot separate these asks the committee to approve a hope (0.7 item 6).
items.pass: Most of the base-case return comes from earnings growth; levers align with what the industry says works (revenue growth, incentives, governance).
items.fail: Return relies on cost cuts or multiple arbitrage.
items.verify: Recompute.

items.request: Stress cases from outside the deal: +200 bp on debt cost and discount rate; stressed advance rates and haircuts; failure of the main bank, lender or counterparty.
items.format: Model scenarios.
items.why: Long-duration assets are rate-sensitive; advance rates and counterparties fail together in a downturn (0.7, 0.11, 0.19).
items.pass: Deal meets debt service and covenants under +200 bp and a counterparty-failure case, or the shortfall is funded.
items.fail: Covenant breach or liquidity shortfall under the stress with no funding plan.
items.verify: Run in our copy of the model.

items.request: Re-underwriting of every debt maturing within 48 months at the current market rate, with the refinancing gap and who funds it.
items.format: Debt schedule and refinance scenario.
items.why: Refinancing walls: legacy coupons near 1% against market near 7% (0.10).
items.pass: Refinance gap is sized and a committed or credible funding source is named.
items.fail: Unfunded refinancing gap.
items.verify: Price indicative refinancing with lenders ourselves.

items.request: Leverage justification: target leverage set against the cash-flow volatility of the business, not what lenders will provide.
items.format: Memo with historical cash-flow volatility and coverage at stressed cash flow.
items.why: About two-thirds of PE firms set leverage at what the market will bear (0.10).
items.pass: Coverage holds at a historical-worst cash-flow year.
items.fail: Leverage justified only by lender appetite.
items.verify: Recompute from historicals.

items.request: Credit agreement and a calculation of maximum permitted leverage under every basket, ratio-debt capacity and EBITDA add-back, against leverage at close.
items.format: Executed or draft credit agreement and our counsel's basket calculation.
items.why: Over 70% of contracts permit senior secured debt above 5x; median agreement has 8 baskets (0.7, 0.10).
items.pass: Maximum permitted leverage is disclosed and does not let priming debt subordinate our position.
items.fail: Maximum permitted far above closing leverage; J.Crew-style unrestricted-subsidiary leakage.
items.verify: Our own counsel reviews baskets, EBITDA definition and unrestricted-subsidiary provisions.

items.request: Synergy table for any M&A or add-on: probability weights and timing, cost synergies separate from revenue synergies, and a dis-synergy line (lost customers and talent).
items.format: Model tab.
items.why: 70% to 90% of deals underperform expectations; revenue synergies take 2 to 3+ years (0.7).
items.pass: Synergies are probability-weighted, timed (cost 1 to 2 years, revenue 2 to 3+), and the deal clears its hurdle without revenue synergies.
items.fail: Unweighted synergies; no dis-synergies.
items.verify: Test with operating diligence.

items.request: Any claimed real-option value (growth options, abandonment value) as a separate, ranged line.
items.format: Model tab with explicit assumptions.
items.why: Option value used to rationalize price (0.6).
items.pass: Deal clears its hurdle without the option line.
items.fail: Price depends on option value.
items.verify: Review assumptions.
