items.test: One person decides on investments, moves cash and reports results, with no independent administrator, custodian or auditor separating those duties.
Sponsor refuses direct, unsolicited confirmation with any bank, administrator, auditor, custodian, prime broker, servicer or processor, or refuses on-site diligence.
Bank, custody or performance statements are available only as sponsor-produced copies and the sponsor will not authorize delivery from the institution.

No accounting function: no in-house CFO or controller, no employee census that reconciles to payroll, or customer assets and matching liabilities not recorded on the balance sheet (the bible calls this an automatic pass).

Any investor, beneficial owner, borrower or counterparty is on the OFAC SDN or sectoral lists, UN, EU or UK lists, or is owned 50% or more in aggregate by blocked persons; or a crypto address in the chain is sanctioned.
Beneficial owners (every 25% owner and a control person) cannot be identified and verified through our own CDD.
Source of funds or source of wealth for the sponsor's commitment or any principal cannot be established with third-party documents.
Distributions or returns to existing investors are funded by new investor money (the definition of a Ponzi), or a fixed or guaranteed above-market return cannot be traced to asset cash flow.
Independent background check finds a material criminal, fraud, securities or regulatory matter that the sponsor or a principal did not disclose in the signed self-disclosure.
Resume, licence, degree or claimed prior exit of a principal is shown to be fabricated or materially inflated.

An undisclosed lien, UCC filing, guarantee, factoring or supply-chain-finance facility is found on the issuer, an affiliate or a principal-owned entity and the sponsor cannot explain why it was omitted.
Customer or fund assets are commingled with personal or sponsor accounts, or used for other ventures.
Bank or administrator wire-approval matrix shows a single person can release funds, or contradicts the sponsor's description and the sponsor cannot reconcile it.
Wire or principal instructions cannot be verified by call-back to an independently obtained number.
Named validators, partners, customers or co-investors deny the relationship or the diligence the sponsor attributed to them.
The sponsor refuses to provide 36 months of bank statements for every account, or the bank confirmations show accounts missing from the set provided.
License cannot be confirmed with the state regulator as real, current, in good standing and transferable (or approvable for the change of control).
Projections deduct ordinary operating expenses federally and the operator will not accept a model rebuilt at full 280E.
Schedule III relief assumed for adult-use revenue, or for medical revenue without a DEA registration, tax opinion and audit-proof apportionment, and value depends on it.
No seed-to-sale compliance trail.
Cash-heavy business that cannot complete proof of cash and segregation-of-duties testing.
License held in a name different from the operating entity with no approved path to align it before closing.
Seller refuses a buy-side QoE, proof of cash on every bank account, or customer calls.
Adjusted EBITDA presented with no bridge from reported net income, or add-backs that cannot be independently validated and the price is not reset to validated EBITDA.

The return does not clear the hurdle with margins flat, the forecast haircut about 20% and exit multiple equal to entry, and the case depends on multiple expansion or margin expansion with no named cost line.
Downside case breaches debt covenants or cannot service debt, including all factoring and supply-chain finance added to leverage.
A known regulatory or data-integrity defect is handled only by the general MAE, with no specific indemnity, closing condition or price adjustment.
Stock consideration or merger partner not diligenced (no independent QoE on the counterparty, auditor not called), or counterparty's auditor resigned recently without explanation.
Data-room hints (volume declines, cancellation letters, rebates) remain unasked or unanswered at signing.

items.check: Hold margins flat in the base case.

items.flag: Return depends on exit multiple above entry.
items.check: Show exit = entry with margins flat, and entry minus 1 to 2 turns.

items.flag: Successor or co-invest offered while the main fund does not take its full pro rata.
items.check: Ask why the GP is syndicating.

items.flag: GP has no voluntary AML program and nobody runs KYC on the other LPs.
items.check: Ask for the AML and sanctions policy and who performs investor KYC.

items.flag: Deck describes a regulatory status that is out of date (for example 'cannabis is now Schedule III' for adult-use).
items.check: Check every 0.18 line at signing.

items.flag: Insured buyers diligencing less because of R&W insurance.
items.check: Remember RWI excludes known matters; diligence to the same floor.

items.flag: Thin diligence by the lead in a hot market (hours falling, competitive round).
items.check: Hold our diligence floor regardless of competition; record intensity.

items.flag: Projections that deduct normal opex federally.
items.check: Rebuild federal tax at full 280E.

items.flag: License in a name different from the operating entity.
items.check: Regulator confirmation of licensee and ownership; change-of-control path.

items.flag: No seed-to-sale compliance trail.
items.check: State tracking-system reports reconciled to inventory and sales.

items.flag: A deck that says 'cannabis is now Schedule III'.
items.check: Correct the model: adult-use is Schedule I; medical relief needs DEA registration and faces pending litigation.

items.flag: Refund claims for prior-year 280E taxes counted in value or liquidity.
items.check: Exclude from value and liquidity.

items.flag: No apportionment method between medical and adult-use for a dual licensee.
items.check: Require a documented apportionment of COGS, revenue and overhead that would survive audit.

items.flag: Exit comps drawn from consumer staples or alcohol with no discount.
items.check: Name eligible buyers; apply sin-stock discount.

items.flag: One bank, short tenure, no backup.
items.check: Bank tenure, closure history, bank's regulatory standing and de-banking contingency plan.

items.flag: COGS includes costs beyond IRC 471 direct costs or claims 263A capitalization.
items.check: Apply the Harborside standard.

items.flag: Margin expansion in a price-compressing state market.
items.check: Hold margins flat in the base case.

items.flag: Risk-factor or legal-proceedings language changed in recent filings without explanation.
items.check: Diff last 8 quarters of filings.

items.flag: Adjusted EBITDA with no bridge.
items.check: Require 3-year bridge from net income to reported, adjusted and pro forma EBITDA with every add-back supported.

items.flag: Cash-basis books, no audited or reviewed financials, inconsistent monthly close.
items.check: QoE with accrual conversion; monthly close history; proof of cash.

items.flag: Seller refuses a buy-side QoE or customer calls.
items.check: Treat as kill test.

items.flag: Retrade risk: valuation and financing not qualified before the LOI.
items.check: Confirm financing commitments and valuation basis before LOI.

items.flag: A seller-imposed deadline used to cut diligence.
items.check: Hold the diligence floor; cooling-off period; walk if scope cannot be completed.

items.flag: Deal champion also owns the valuation model.
items.check: Separate valuation team; walk-away price set by someone off the deal team.

items.flag: A history of budgets missed optimistically.
items.check: Compare last three budgets with actuals; treat as fraud precursor.

items.flag: Factoring or supply-chain finance excluded from leverage.
items.check: Add every facility to leverage; UCC sweep across all secured parties.

items.flag: Period-end balances that differ sharply from intra-quarter averages.
items.check: Average daily balances of cash, debt and receivables; flag financing unwinding after period-end (Repo 105).

items.flag: References in the data room to volume declines, cancellation letters or rebates nobody has asked about.
items.check: Written question log; ask in customer meetings; re-run the model.

items.flag: A non-functional whistleblower hotline, or no hotline log.
items.check: Call or email the hotline during diligence; request 3-year hotline log.

items.flag: A known regulatory defect handled only by the general MAE.
items.check: Specific indemnity or closing condition for each known issue.

items.flag: Monitoring agreement with fee acceleration on exit.
items.check: Read sponsor fee agreements; require removal or full disclosure and LPA offset.

items.flag: A return case that needs exit multiple above entry, or margin expansion with no named cost line.
items.check: Run the attribution test (flat margins, exit at entry).

items.flag: Stock consideration from a buyer whose auditor recently resigned.
items.check: Call the counterparty's auditors; own QoE on the counterparty.

items.flag: No-poach clauses in franchise or vendor agreements.
items.check: Clause review; confirm removal; open AG or class-action exposure.

items.flag: Sponsor doubling deal pace without doubling its operating bench.
items.check: Chart sponsor deals per year against team size.

items.flag: Sponsor claims to close a much larger share of opportunities than about 6 per 100, or calls a banked deal proprietary.
items.check: Ask who else saw it and whether a banker ran a process.

items.flag: Value-creation plan that relies mainly on cost cuts or multiple arbitrage.
items.check: Lever split against sponsors' own ratings (cost reduction important in only 36% of deals pre-deal).

items.flag: IPO-dependent exit.
items.check: IPOs are under 20% of exits; model strategic and financial-buyer exits.

items.flag: Leverage set at 'as much as the market will bear' rather than by cash-flow volatility.
items.check: Justify leverage from cash-flow volatility; compare to SR 13-3 6x concern level.

items.flag: Revenue in one currency and debt in another, or reliance on a currency peg.
items.check: Currency-mismatch stress test.

items.flag: Sale-leaseback or dividend recap proceeds paid out with escalating rent left behind.
items.check: Model rent coverage post-leaseback; trace proceeds (Steward).

items.flag: Clean public search used as evidence of no misconduct.
items.check: Request internal investigations log; public databases capture about 1/64 of substantiated misconduct.

items.flag: Insured buyer reduces diligence because R&W is in place.
items.check: Hold the same diligence floor; insurer excludes what is known and disputes what should have been found.

items.flag: Lenders' counsel designated by the sponsor and no independent review of baskets, EBITDA definition or unrestricted subsidiaries.
items.check: Own counsel review; require J.Crew blocker.

items.flag: Buying more debt in a company where we already hold equity.
items.check: Do not be wrong twice; separate credit decision.

items.flag: Healthcare or government-reimbursed target with falling staffing hours or rising fee, lease and interest leakage to the sponsor or landlord.
items.check: Model staffing and quality metrics and fee, lease and interest leakage.

items.question: What are the first three things you look at in a deal like this, and what makes you stop reading?
items.good_answer: A specific, ranked list tied to the deal's failure modes (cash, collateral, sponsor), with a kill test they have actually applied.

items.question: What do you ask for that sponsors rarely have ready, and can you give it to us now?
items.good_answer: They produce the A.6 first-request items (36 months of bank statements, bank-confirmed wire matrix, average balances, off-balance-sheet financing list) promptly and completely.

items.question: What does a deck in this asset class most often get wrong, and how does yours avoid it?
items.good_answer: Names a concrete error (exit multiple, margin expansion, stale marks) and shows the corresponding sensitivity in the model.

items.question: Which numbers did you rebuild yourself and which did you take from management or a seller?
items.good_answer: Lists rebuilt numbers with the source documents, and names the figures taken on trust with the rep that covers each.

items.question: Tell us about a deal that looked clean and went bad. What did you miss?
items.good_answer: A specific case, the variable misjudged, and the process change made afterwards.

items.question: Which third-party reports have you commissioned, who engaged each provider, and may we speak to them?
items.good_answer: Reports engaged by an independent party, with engagement letters and consent to call the providers.

items.question: Which terms are non-negotiable for you, and why?
items.good_answer: Investor-protective terms (information, audit, consent rights) rather than sponsor-protective ones.

items.question: Whose diligence are you relying on, and what would make you trust it?
items.good_answer: They rely on no one else's diligence without verifying its scope and hours, and can say what they checked themselves.

items.question: How many hours did you spend with management in person, how many sites did you visit, and how many references did you call?
items.good_answer: Specific numbers at or above the floor (about 10 references; meaningful in-person hours), and what was skipped for timing.

items.question: Describe a decision process you changed after a loss.
items.good_answer: A concrete post-mortem and the resulting change.

items.question: When did you last decline a hot deal or manager on operational grounds alone?
items.good_answer: A dated example with the operational issue that drove the decline.

items.question: How do you size the haircut to management's forecast, and how has it compared with outcomes?
items.good_answer: An explicit haircut (around 20% median) calibrated against their own forecast record.

items.question: Who set the walk-away price, and is that person on the deal team?
items.good_answer: A walk-away set before bidding by someone separate from the deal champions.

items.question: Which of the statements you received were contradicted by third-party records?
items.good_answer: Specific examples and how each was resolved, showing they check against third-party records.

items.question: When did you last test a whistleblower hotline, here or at a portfolio company, and what happened?
items.good_answer: They have tested it, it worked, and they can show hotline statistics.

items.question: Show us the amendment history of every credit agreement and LPA.
items.good_answer: A complete amendment log with reasons; no serial extensions hiding losses.

items.question: How do you dedupe collateral against other lenders' borrowing bases?
items.good_answer: Item-level dedupe (invoice, VIN, serial) across all facilities by an independent collateral agent, plus a UCC sweep across affiliates.

items.question: What share of your last ten deals changed CEO, and when did you first know?
items.good_answer: A number near the base rate (69%), with early identification and a successor bench.

items.question: Why are you offering this co-investment, and is the main fund taking its full pro rata?
items.good_answer: Main fund takes its full pro rata; syndication is for size or concentration, with a rule-based allocation policy.

items.question: Who chose lender counsel on your last three financings, and what did independent counsel change?
items.good_answer: Independent counsel for lenders; specific changes to baskets or EBITDA definitions.

items.question: What is your fixed-fee share of revenue in a downside, and do fees keep the lights on without carry?
items.good_answer: A fee base that funds the team in a downside without depending on new fundraising.

items.question: Which default definition do you report, and what is your realized loss rate?
items.good_answer: Names the definition (payment, covenant, realized loss) and gives the realized loss with source.

items.question: If your bank closed this morning, how many weeks of payroll could you meet?
items.good_answer: A specific number of weeks from cash held in multiple banks, insured sweeps or Treasury MMFs.

items.question: Who can release a wire, and will your bank confirm that list to us directly?
items.good_answer: At least two signatories with an independent approver, and immediate consent to bank confirmation.

items.question: Who has write access to pricing inputs and valuation models?
items.good_answer: Nobody on the investment team; the administrator or independent valuer controls inputs, with access logs.

items.question: What did your QoE not test, and did proof of cash cover every account on the bank confirmations?
items.good_answer: Reads out the scope exclusions and confirms full account coverage.

items.question: Who else saw this deal, and did a banker run a process?
items.good_answer: Names the intermediary and other bidders; the claim can be corroborated.

items.question: What is your annual deployment target, and what share of the market is that?
items.good_answer: A modest share of the market with a record of declining deals to stay selective.

items.question: Justify the leverage by this business's cash-flow volatility, not by lender appetite.
items.good_answer: Coverage computed at the worst historical cash-flow year.

items.question: What is the maximum leverage the documents permit, including every basket and add-back?
items.good_answer: A computed figure close to closing leverage, with blockers on unrestricted subsidiaries.

items.question: Do you run an AML program, who performs KYC on your other investors, and does anyone file SARs?
items.good_answer: A written program with a named owner and administrator KYC, despite no federal requirement until 2028.

items.question: Restate each term of art in your deck in one sentence with a number.
items.good_answer: Every term restated precisely, tying to the model.

items.question: What return do you get with exit multiple equal to entry and margins flat, and at entry minus 1 to 2 turns?
items.good_answer: The deal still clears its hurdle at exit = entry and flat margins; the lower case is shown without prompting.

items.question: What must be true for this price: margin, growth and exit multiple on a fully diluted count?
items.good_answer: Implied figures within the range achieved by peers.

items.question: Show the track record with and without your top one or two deals, as PME.
items.good_answer: Record remains above benchmark without the top outcomes, computed from LP cash flows.

items.question: Which partners produced the track record, and are they still here and leading this deal?
items.good_answer: The responsible partners are still present and on this deal.

items.question: If the founder stepped back tomorrow, who decides, who owns investor relationships, and what happens to economics?
items.good_answer: A formal succession plan with a successor who has led at scale.

items.question: Can the CEO execute this specific plan, how fast can gaps close, who are the successors, and how will requirements change over the hold?
items.good_answer: Evidence-based answers to all four questions and a named successor.

items.question: Which validators, partners, customers or co-investors have you named, and may we call each directly?
items.good_answer: Full list with contacts and unconditional consent.

items.question: Where is every claim on this asset, and who sees all of them?
items.good_answer: A single schedule reconciled to UCC and title searches, monitored by an independent agent.

items.question: Is any financing excluded from leverage: factoring, supply-chain finance, receivables sales, inventory finance, guarantees?
items.good_answer: None excluded; all added to leverage in the consolidated look-through.

items.question: Where are we in the cycle for this asset, and who buys it at exit once new supply arrives?
items.good_answer: A scorecard-based answer naming the exit buyer and the multiple they will pay.

items.question: Which regulatory status lines does this deal rely on, and are they current?
items.good_answer: Accurate November 2026 status for each, checked by counsel.

items.question: What would the post-mortem say if this deal lost half its value in three years?
items.good_answer: A candid scenario naming the most likely failure variable and the monitoring that would catch it early.

items.question: Have you ever been asked to do something with invoices, payments or records that felt wrong? (to employees, vendors, customers)
items.good_answer: No, with specifics on how such requests would be escalated.

items.question: For every hint in the data room (lost customers, volume cuts, auditor changes), what did you ask, and what was the answer?
items.good_answer: A complete hints log with written questions, answers, askers and model updates.

items.question: Is any revenue dependent on a government decision, and what happens if it is cancelled or swept?
items.good_answer: Termination and sweep modelled at first opportunity with the deal still viable.

items.question: Can you obtain bindable insurance for the full hold, and what happens at twice the premium?
items.good_answer: Bindable quotes in hand and a model that survives a 2x premium.

items.question: Which of your metrics could be gamed (NRR, adjusted EBITDA, ACV, DSCR, IRR), and will you give us the raw data to recompute each?
items.good_answer: Raw data delivered for every headline metric, with definitions that match the recomputation.

items.question: What is the single check that, if it fails, kills this deal?
items.good_answer: Names it unprompted and shows the evidence that it passes.

items.question: Which of your claims did you verify yourself and which are assertions?
items.good_answer: A claims register separating verified (with verifier) from asserted.

items.question: Is any DSCR computed on anticipated rather than in-place leases, and is the cap rate NOI-based or cash-flow-based?
items.good_answer: DSCR on in-place leases; cap rate NOI-based and stated.

items.question: Does any redemption right exceed liquidity coverage (cash + NII + maturities against the cap)?
items.good_answer: Coverage computed and above the cap with history of meeting requests.

items.question: Which numbers here are period-end snapshots, and what are the averages?
items.good_answer: Averages provided for every balance-sheet figure, consistent with period-end.

items.question: Which short-term funding lines do you rely on, and what happens at a 50% haircut?
items.good_answer: Each line listed with stressed haircut and the unencumbered liquidity that covers the call.

items.question: Specialist (utilities and data-center lenders): how is non-firm or flexible interconnection treated in the lease and debt documents, and how many curtailment hours are underwritten?
items.good_answer: Explicit curtailment-hour assumptions in both lease and debt documents with rent and DSCR tested at those hours.

items.question: Specialist (crypto custody auditors): who supplies the proof-of-reserves challenge, which liabilities are covered, and what is the audit scope?
items.good_answer: Challenge supplied by an independent party, full customer liabilities covered, same-block reserves and liabilities, and a defined scope.

items.question: Specialist (insurance regulators or rating analysts): how do you consolidate RBC across affiliated captives and private placements?
items.good_answer: Consolidated statutory view including captives, with independent valuation of affiliated placements.

items.question: Specialist (real estate lenders): what LTC and DSCR do you actually lend at, by deal size, and what promote structures do you see?
items.good_answer: Specific current figures by deal size, with federal-program ceilings (HUD 87% LTC at 1.15x) treated as ceilings, not norms.

items.question: Specialist (venture investors): at what ARR does the Rule of 40 start to matter more than NRR in your pricing?
items.good_answer: A stated threshold (ICONIQ: about $25M ARR) and evidence from their own pricing.

items.question: What is federal tax at full 280E, and what does the model assume?
items.good_answer: A model rebuilt at full 280E on every dollar of revenue as base case, with any relief shown separately as upside.

items.question: Which revenue is medical, which adult-use, and how is overhead apportioned?
items.good_answer: Revenue by license type from the seed-to-sale and POS systems, with a documented apportionment of COGS, revenue and overhead that a tax opinion supports.

items.question: Do you hold a DEA registration under the new pathway? Show it.
items.good_answer: The registration certificate, confirmed with DEA, covering the medical activity claimed.

items.question: Who wrote the tax opinion, and what does it assume about IRS treatment?
items.good_answer: A named independent tax counsel opinion that states its assumptions about IRS treatment absent guidance and covers the apportionment.

items.question: Are any prior-year refund claims in the numbers?
items.good_answer: No; or they are removed from value and liquidity.

items.question: May we call the state regulator to confirm license standing and change-of-control approval?
items.good_answer: Yes, with a signed authorization and the regulator's contact.

items.question: Who is your bank, for how long, and what happens if it closes the account tomorrow?
items.good_answer: Named bank with multi-year tenure, no closure history and a tested backup banking relationship and cash-handling plan.

items.question: Who can legally buy this company at exit, and at what multiple?
items.good_answer: A named buyer pool legally permitted to own plant-touching assets, with comps discounted from consumer staples.

items.question: Is COGS limited to IRC 471 direct costs?
items.good_answer: Yes: a COGS build excluding 263A capitalization, consistent with Harborside.

items.question: Which reported earnings survive the close? Show the bridge.
items.good_answer: A 3-year bridge from reported net income to reported, adjusted and pro forma EBITDA, each add-back documented and independently validated, reconciled to cash.

items.question: How was the NWC peg built, and what was excluded?
items.good_answer: Trailing 12-month average of normalized NWC with seasonality modeled, definition excluding cash, debt and income tax, every exclusion listed.

items.question: Split the return: how much is growth, paydown and multiple? How much is from recaps?
items.good_answer: An attribution table separating revenue growth, margin change, debt paydown, multiple change and recap proceeds.

items.question: What happens to the debt in the downside case?
items.good_answer: Downside with flat or lower margins and exit at entry minus 1 to 2 turns that still services debt and passes covenants, with headroom stated.

items.question: What is our walk-away price, who set it, and is that person on the deal team?
items.good_answer: A walk-away price set from conservative cash flows before bidding by someone outside the deal team.

items.question: Which synergies are cost and which are revenue? What is each one's probability and timing? What are the dis-synergies?
items.good_answer: A synergy table with probability and timing per line and a dis-synergy line for lost customers and talent.

items.question: What contingent liabilities (litigation, data breach, product) did diligence price, and how?
items.good_answer: A contingent-liability model including mass-tort and successor exposure, with each item priced or specifically indemnified.

items.question: What did the QoE engagement letter exclude, and which bank accounts were not in proof of cash?
items.good_answer: The engagement letter scope section, a list of procedures not performed, and confirmation that every account in the bank confirmations was in proof of cash.

items.question: How do the last three budgets compare with actuals?
items.good_answer: Budget vs actual for three years showing misses that are not consistently optimistic, with explanations.

items.question: For every hint in the data room, what question did we ask, who asked it, and what was the answer?
items.good_answer: A written question log with each hint, the person who asked, the counterparty answer, and the model change.

items.question: What is maximum permitted senior secured leverage under the baskets, against closing leverage?
items.good_answer: A computation summing all incurrence baskets, ratio debt and EBITDA add-backs, compared with closing leverage.

items.question: What does the return look like with exit multiple equal to entry and margins flat?
items.good_answer: The attribution-test return and the share of the sponsor case that survives, still clearing the hurdle.

items.question: Can this CEO execute this plan, and who is the successor?
items.good_answer: An assessment against the four questions (execute this plan, close gaps fast, credible successors, changing requirements) with named internal and external successors and an extended-hold downside if a change is likely.

items.question: What did diligence find that the R&W policy will therefore exclude, and how is it priced?
items.good_answer: A list mapping each finding to the policy exclusion and to a price reduction or specific indemnity.

items.question: When did we last call the hotline, and what happened?
items.good_answer: A dated test of the hotline during diligence with a logged, timely response.

items.question: How much uncalled capital does the owning fund hold for this company in a downturn?
items.good_answer: Uncalled capital and reserve policy documented for the owning fund, sufficient for a downside equity cure.

items.question: What is net cash per share after expected redemptions?
items.good_answer: A computation: (trust cash after redemptions minus merger costs minus warrant value) divided by shares including promote.

items.question: Who prepared the projections, and who owes us a duty on them?
items.good_answer: Projections prepared or tested by our own advisors, with specific reps from the counterparty on facts we cannot verify.

items.question: Has the counterparty's auditor changed in three years?
items.good_answer: No; or a full explanation confirmed by calling both auditors.

items.question: When does our fraud claim expire?
items.good_answer: A diary with the fraud limitations period and indemnity survival dates for every rep.

items.question: Who else saw this deal, and did a banker run a process?
items.good_answer: Names of the banker and other bidders, consistent with the funnel and sourcing base rates.

items.question: What is the efforts definition in the earnout, and how does it bind the buyer after the first milestone?
items.good_answer: A commercially reasonable efforts definition that applies to every milestone, with spend commitments and reporting and audit rights.
